company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates with $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but quality was low — the beat was driven by tariff refunds (145 basis point tailwind to gross margins) and a non-cash LIFO impact (105 basis point tailwind). Domestic comps disappointed at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal expands Cognex's footprint in the fast-growing robotics and AI perception space.

MillerKnoll delivered solid FQ1 EPS upside at 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and importantly would have beaten even without tariff refunds (adjusted EPS of 42 cents vs. 36 cents expected). Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed slightly to $3.88-4.03 billion, but the EPS band was held unchanged at $1.85-2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership/operational item with no financial guidance change.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates with 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the 13.85% expected, despite revenue coming in slightly above at $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures weighing on retail, with significant gross margin pressure from rising material costs. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a ~75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. The results represent a significant data point in the competitive GLP-1 obesity drug landscape. This is a major positive catalyst for the stock and could drive sector-wide attention to GLP-1 competitors.

sectors: GLP-1 obesity drug space in focus after Viking Therapeutics reported 22% weight loss in VK2735 trial, likely drawing attention to the broader weight loss drug sector and competitors. RV industry sentiment remains cautious per THOR Industries commentary on macro headwinds weighing on consumer discretionary spending.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, so there's no broad macro or rates commentary today — this one is all about the individual movers reporting before the open.

Let's start with the biggest mover. Viking Therapeutics is spiking in pre-market after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug VK2735, with patients showing 22% weight loss. That's a headline number that will get attention across the obesity drug space and put pressure on competitors. This is the most market-moving item of the morning.

AutoZone beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings at $56.05 per share versus the Street at $54.03, but the quality of that beat is questionable. The upside was driven by tariff refunds — a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins — and a non-cash LIFO accounting benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the underlying business was soft. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the 3.1% expected, and operating expenses as a percent of sales worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity toward the end of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027, but this is a low-quality beat that the market may not fully reward.

Cognex announced it is acquiring RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and physical AI applications, for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus another 106 million. RealSense is expected to generate 80 to 90 million dollars in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on the robotics and AI perception theme and should be read as bullish for Cognex.

MillerKnoll posted a genuine earnings beat — 53 cents per share versus 36 cents expected — and management made a point of noting they would have beaten even without tariff refunds, with adjusted earnings of 42 cents. Sales missed at $923 million versus the $943 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed modestly, but the EPS band was left unchanged. Call it mixed with a slight positive lean on profit quality.

THOR Industries missed on fiscal fourth quarter earnings with 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the 13.85% the Street was modeling. Management's tone was cautious, citing stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation weighing on household budgets. On the positive side, dealer inventory is healthy and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year. Still, this is a miss with weak forward commentary.

Pentair named a new permanent CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st, bringing experience from prior CFO roles at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership move, no guidance change.

Bottom line: Viking is the standout this morning in the GLP-1 space. AutoZone's beat is noisy. Cognex's acquisition is strategically sound. THO is the clearest disappointment. Stay focused on the Viking move for sector ripple effects throughout the session.
